espn-603993.headline: Contepomi makes twelve changes to end eleven years
beats: Argentina have not beaten Ireland in eleven years. Ireland have won nine of the last ten, and the one that still rankles is the 2015 World Cup quarter-final. Felipe Contepomi has changed 12 of the side that drew with Australia in September and goes full strength in Dublin.
Argentina's last two Tests were both against Australia: lost 21–27, then drew 28–28 a week later. Ireland have not played since July, when New Zealand put 40 on them.
Dan Sheehan captains Ireland at the Aviva for the first time and calls talk of decline "nonsense". Lose, and Ireland drop to fourth in the world, below France.
Both then meet sides without a point in the championship, Ireland hosting Fiji and Argentina away to Italy. Whoever loses here gets a soft landing, which is not the same as an answer.

espn-603994.headline: Italy are 16 short; South Africa took it seriously
beats: Italy name their side with 16 players missing and Giacomo Nicotera as captain. Gonzalo Quesada takes South Africa's selection as a compliment: “They’ll field their strongest possible side; it’s a sign of great respect towards us”.
Italy have not played since July, when Australia beat them 57–10 away in the Nations Championship. South Africa's last visit, on 15 November 2025, ended 14–32.

South Africa's version of short-handed is Salmaan Moerat, who has captained them four times, standing in for the injured Eben Etzebeth. Italy's answer includes Ross Vintcent, born in South Africa and raised on its rugby, and Monty Ioane on his 50th cap.
Quesada wants Italy unpredictable. Beating the unbeaten championship leaders from here would qualify, and would hand New Zealand first place in the world rankings without them lifting a finger.

espn-603995.headline: Scotland have tried 33 times. Here is the 34th.
beats: Not one of the previous 33 meetings has gone Scotland's way, a run that stretches back 121 years. Last November they lost 17–25 at home, and Gregor Townsend says his side have gone back to that game.

Scotland have not played since beating Fiji 33–17 in July. New Zealand lost three straight to South Africa, then put 50 and 43 on Australia in October, and Townsend sees a side "playing much more ambitious rugby".
Finn Russell and captain Sione Tuipulotu start, Russell on his 96th cap. Lose by 16 or more and Scotland drop below Australia in the rankings, a week before they host them.
Jeff Wilson, an All Blacks great, says only "bizarre officiating" can stop New Zealand. After 33 attempts, Scotland are not fussy about how.

espn-603996.headline: A point short in Cardiff, Japan bring a Welshman
beats: Japan lost 24–23 here on 15 November 2025, a few months after beating Wales in Kitakyushu. The former Wales international Kingsley Jones was in their camp before both games, and he is in it again now.
Eddie Jones says of his friend: "I don't think he's stopped talking the whole time." The advice goes to a side that hands a debut at flyhalf to the uncapped Riku Kitahara.

Wales last played in July and lost 43–0 to South Africa without scoring a try. Steve Tandy starts Sam Costelow at 10 and pairs Max Llewellyn with Eddie James, his sixth midfield in 13 Tests. Lose by any margin and Wales fall below Italy and Japan in the world rankings.
A week later Wales host New Zealand and Japan go to England. Last time a point separated them. Neither side can count on many more this month.

espn-603997.headline: Fiji's new number eight has 22 England caps
beats: Nathan Hughes is 35 and Fiji-born, and he won those caps between 2016 and 2019. World Rugby's revised rule on switching allegiance after three years away puts him in Jake White's back row for White's second game in charge.

France are short of bodies. Meafou, Flament, Jalibert and Brau-Boirie are out for November, and Oscar Jegou cracked a rib in training. Antoine Dupont captains, and Kalvin Gourgues gets a first start after four caps off the bench.
Fiji's last Nations Championship game against England, at home in July, finished 8–73. They come to Lyon on a 34–28 win over Japan, still without a point in this competition.
Win, and Fiji push France below England in the world rankings. That would be an odd favour from a man whose last England cap came in 2019.

espn-603998.headline: Australia bring a fixed defence and an unfixed pay row
beats: Australia conceded 50 and 43 to New Zealand in October. Angus Bell says the Wallabies have "addressed and fixed those issues" since, which is the easier of their two problems.
The other is at home. Rugby Australia claim the players' union's proposals "threaten the future of the game", a year out from a World Cup on their own turf.

England have not played since beating Argentina 31–24 in July, and won the last meeting 25–7 at home a year ago. They have back-row trouble of their own. Tom Curry is a major doubt, Pepper and Underhill are already out, and twin Ben, who has not played for England since 2025, is in the frame to start.
An Australian win would lift them to fifth in the world and drop England to seventh, below Scotland. Australia play Scotland next, so they would at least know where they stand.

espn-603999.headline: Win here and France make New Zealand world No. 1
beats: South Africa have been first in the world rankings since 31 August. Any France win at Stade de France drops them to second, behind New Zealand, and lifts France above Ireland into third.
The last meeting went the other way: South Africa won 32–17 in Saint-Denis on 8 November 2025. This year they beat New Zealand three times running at home, then conceded 42 to Australia in September.
France score freely and give it back. They managed at least four tries in each of their last five Tests and still lost two of them, 40–50 in Scotland and 32–34 in New Zealand.
South Africa also lead the Nations Championship only on points difference, level with New Zealand on 15. New Zealand stand to gain from this one without lifting a finger.

espn-604000.headline: Italy last won in March. Argentina in July.
beats: Italy's last win was 23–18 over England at home in the Six Nations. Since then, four losses, the last 57–10 in Australia. Argentina beat Wales 35–21 in July and have not won in four since, a run that ends in a 28–28 draw with Australia.

Both arrive from bigger appointments. Italy meet South Africa in Turin on 7 November, where Gonzalo Quesada said "Dobbiamo provare a essere imprevedibili": they must try to be unpredictable. Argentina go to Dublin first, and Felipe Contepomi has made 12 changes from the side that drew with Australia.
Win, and Italy climb to ninth in the world, above Fiji and Wales. Argentina stay eighth whatever happens, which leaves them only the drought to lose.
Fiji come to Italy a week later, also on no points. Argentina are the harder way to get off zero.

espn-604001.headline: Wales will need more than a hat trick this time
beats: On 22 November 2025 Tom Rogers became the first Wales player to score a hat trick against New Zealand. Wales still lost 52–26 in Cardiff, and the All Blacks extended a winning streak against Wales that was then 72 years old.
Wales last played in July and lost 43–0 in South Africa without scoring a try. New Zealand's last two Tests produced 50 and 43 points against Australia, with seven tries in each.
A Wales win would lift them to ninth in the world, above Fiji, a side they beat 39–24 in July and still trail.
New Zealand are level on points with South Africa at the top of the Nations Championship, and England come next. A loss in Cardiff would cost them more than a streak.

espn-604002.headline: England have sat fifth since July. Japan can move them
beats: England have been fifth in every World Rugby table since 13 July. Japan were ninth as recently as October and have been twelfth since losing 28–34 to Fiji at home, a month after beating them.

England's run since March reads like two different sides. They lost 18–23 in Italy and 21–45 in South Africa, then scored 16 tries in two July wins, 73–8 in Fiji and 31–24 in Argentina. A Japan win would still drop them to seventh, below Scotland and Australia, and England host Australia on this ground a week earlier.
Japan reach London by way of Cardiff, where Eddie Jones set out to make Japan the first side from his country to beat Wales there.
After this, England host New Zealand and Japan go to Scotland. The ranking England have held since July is easiest to lose in the week that looks easiest.

espn-604003.headline: Ireland can only lose ground against Fiji
beats: Ireland have been third in the world since July, and beating Fiji by any margin keeps them exactly there. It is the only result that does. Anything less hands third to France.

Dan Sheehan, captaining again for the injured Caelan Doris, calls talk of an Irish decline "nonsense". The talk has a source: double-digit defeats by South Africa, New Zealand and France, the latest 21–40 away to New Zealand in July.

Fiji are last in the pool without a point, and conceded 73 at home to England in July. They did win their last game, 34–28 away to Japan. Their real target is Italy, also pointless, away the following week.
Ireland ran in eight tries against Fiji here in November 2024, winning 52–17. A repeat proves little. South Africa come to Dublin a week later, and that is where Sheehan's word gets tested.

espn-604004.headline: Two leaky defences, one ranking place to swap
beats: Australia conceded 50 and 43 to New Zealand in a fortnight in October. Scotland's way of winning this year has been to outscore people, beating France 50–40 and Argentina 47–38.

The Wallabies reach Edinburgh by way of England at Twickenham. They are a year from a home World Cup, in a pay dispute in which Rugby Australia claims the players' union's proposals threaten the future of the game.
Sixth hosts seventh, and the gap is small enough that any Australian win puts them above Scotland. For a side that has just let in 93 points to one opponent, that is a generous offer.

Australia have won 22 of the 35 meetings. Townsend, who once spent an amateur summer playing club rugby in Sydney, has had some of the most free-scoring games of his nine years in charge against them. Neither defence suggests that is about to stop.
